title: The Bank Guarantee Behind Imvo Zabantsundu's First Issue in 1884
conflicts: Lovedale exit and election: 1884 and 1883 respectively in the 1922 biography (quoting R. W. Rose-Innes) versus 1883 and 1884 in the HSRC chapter; story says 'by 1884' and leaves the election undated. Launch day: 3 November 1884 (Press Council, quoting the first issue) versus 4 November in some summaries; story uses 3 November. 'First Black-owned': Press Council says first Black-owned and controlled; UCT archive and Vuk'uzenzele say first independent Black newspaper; SAHO's 'first Bantu-language newspaper' is wrong and not used. Story describes the white guarantors' role rather than claiming sole ownership from day one.
notes: Main narrative source is D. D. T. Jabavu's 1922 biography of his father (public domain, Internet Archive), which quotes Richard Rose-Innes at length; corroborated by the HSRC chapter (via The Journalist) and the Press Council article. The later critique of dependence on liberal backers is attributed to scholars. Jabavu's later politics (1898 Bond pact, 1913 Land Act) are outside the episode and not covered.
